name: Zeitz Museum of Contemporary Art Africa (Zeitz MOCAA)
region: V&A Waterfront · Cape Town · South Africa
subtitle: Zeitz MOCAA is a public, not-for-profit museum in Cape Town that exhibits, collects and researches contemporary art from Africa and its diaspora.

facts.label: What
facts.value: A public, not-for-profit museum that exhibits, collects, preserves and researches contemporary art from Africa and its diaspora.

facts.label: Building
facts.value: The museum is housed in a 1920s grain silo transformed by Heatherwick Studio.

facts.label: Building
facts.value: Light enters the atrium through tubes 5.5 metres wide.

facts.label: Cost and funder
facts.value: The conversion cost more than R500 million, borne by the V&A Waterfront corporation.

facts.label: Collection
facts.value: The core of the holdings is Jochen Zeitz's art collection, built up since 2008 with South African curator Mark Coetzee; it gave Zeitz the naming rights.

facts.label: Galleries
facts.value: More than 80 cube-like gallery spaces are clustered around the atrium.

facts.label: Criticism
facts.value: Art critic Sean O'Toole said the collection has 'crucial blind spots'.

parts.text: Zeitz MOCAA is a public, not-for-profit museum in Cape Town that exhibits, collects and researches contemporary art from Africa and its diaspora. It occupies a 1920s grain silo converted by Heatherwick Studio, and its holdings were built on Jochen Zeitz's private collection. Critics have questioned gaps in the collection and the overlap between museum and private acquisitions.
